title: fix(vllm): unblock Qwen3.5 hybrid decode
body:
## Description

Running qwen3.5-35b-a3b (hybrid GDN/Mamba + full-attention) through maxtext.inference.vllm_decode crashed before a single token could be produced.

Two independent bugs were hit back to back:

1.
```bash 
TypeError: KVCacheManager._maybe_set_compact_mamba_num_blocks_override() missing 3 required positional arguments`:           

'num_attn_groups', 'num_mamba_groups', and 'group_size'

```
2. 
```bash
TypeError: Qwen3_5ScannableBlock.__call__() got an unexpected keyword argument 'kv_cache'
```

### Scope of the impact:

Only hybrid models routed through the adapter's hybrid KV-cache patch are affected, i.e. `decoder_block: qwen3_next` and `decoder_block: qwen3_5`.
- `qwen3_next` was already wired for external KV caches, so bug 2 is Qwen3.5-specific.
- Dense models such as `qwen3-30b-a3b` reach neither code path (`decoder_block: qwen3_moe`, `inhomogeneous_layer_cycle_interval: 1`) and are unaffected.
- Bug 1 hits Qwen3.5 regardless of `scan_layers`; bug 2 only hits `scan_layers=True`.

## Root Cause

### Bug 1 — cross-version signature drift on `_maybe_set_compact_mamba_num_blocks_override`

`tpu_inference.runner.kv_cache_manager.KVCacheManager` changed the signature of `_maybe_set_compact_mamba_num_blocks_override` between releases:

| revision | signature |
| :--- | :--- |
| tpu-inference @ HEAD | `(attn_page_size_bytes, unpadded_mamba_page_size_bytes, num_attn_layers, num_mamba_layers)` |
| tpu-inference shipped in the Pathways/vLLM images (`tpu_inference==0.29.0`) | `(attn_page_size_bytes, unpadded_mamba_page_size_bytes, num_attn_groups, num_mamba_groups, num_attn_layers, num_mamba_layers, group_size)` |

The adapter calls this private method from its hybrid KV-cache patch and was pinned to the newer 4-argument form, so it blew up on any image carrying the older 7-argument form. MaxText has no way to know which of the two it is linked against at import time, and both are in active use today, so hard-coding either one is wrong.

### Bug 2 — the Qwen3.5 scanned path was never wired for external KV caches

Two layered problems:

- `Qwen3_5ScannableBlock.__call__` accepted neither `kv_cache` nor `attention_metadata`. `nnx_decoders._apply_layers_sequentially` filters the kwargs it forwards using `inspect.signature(layer_cls.__call__)` and injects `kv_cache` separately, so the block raised a `TypeError` the moment vLLM supplied caches. (`Qwen3NextScannableBlock` already had the equivalent  `_forward_with_external_kv_cache` plumbing; Qwen3.5 never got it.)
- Even with the parameter added, the counts do not line up. Qwen3.5-35B has 40 decoder layers with `inhomogeneous_layer_cycle_interval: 4`, so one scan step is a 4-layer block and there are only 10 blocks, while vLLM hands back 40 caches — one per layer. The generic scanned branch in `nnx_decoders` passed that flat 40-element list through unchanged, so block `i` would have received cache `i` instead of layers `4i .. 4i+3`.

## Solution

### Bug 1 — filter kwargs by the callee's real signature.

- New helper `call_with_supported_kwargs(func, **kwargs)` in `src/maxtext/integration/vllm/hybrid_cache_utils.py`. It `inspects inspect.signature(func)`, forwards everything when the callee declares `**kwargs`, drops (and logs) the kwargs the callee does not declare, and still lets a genuinely unsatisfiable call raise `TypeError` rather than masking it.
- The adapter now computes all seven values and delegates the filtering, so the same MaxText build works against both tpu-inference revisions.
- The helper lives in `hybrid_cache_utils.py` rather than `adapter.py` because that module does not import `tpu_inference`, which keeps it importable and unit-testable on CPU.

### Bug 2 — thread per-sublayer caches through the block, regroup in the decoder.

- `Qwen3_5ScannableBlock.__call__ ` now takes `kv_cache` and `attention_metadata`, hands `kv_cache[i]` to `layer_i` (bounds-guarded with `i < len(kv_cache)`), collects the updated caches, and returns `(x, tuple(updated_kv_caches))`. When `kv_cache is None` it returns `(x, None)`, so the training path is byte-for-byte unchanged.
- `nnx_decoders` gained an `is_qwen3_5` flag and, in the generic scanned branch, regroups the flat per-layer list into per-block tuples before the scan and flattens it back afterwards, reusing the existing `maxtext_utils.prepare_kv_caches_for_scan` / `update_kv_caches_after_scan` helpers. This is gated on `self.is_qwen3_5 and cycle_interval > 1`, so no other model's behaviour moves.

Deliberate design note: `_apply_qwen3_next_scanned_blocks` was not reused, even though it looks superficially applicable. It passes `skip_block_remat=True` because `Qwen3NextScannableBlock` rematerializes its own sub-layers internally. `Qwen3_5ScannableBlock` is a plain `for` loop with no internal remat, so reusing that path would have silently disabled rematerialization for Qwen3.5. Only the cache grouping helpers are shared.


# Tests

Qwen3.5-35b `vllm_decode` before RL training: https://cloudlogging.app.goo.gl/zx1kpgx3ke2dgUow5
Qwen3.5-35b RL training: https://cloudlogging.app.goo.gl/UZiCeMgXSj6ceZkD9
Qwen3.5-35b `vllm_decode` after RL training: https://cloudlogging.app.goo.gl/wgicekjYZRBoyMru7

title: Add default artifact registry repository name to Github workflow
body:
# Description

This PR fixes an issue where scheduled Docker image builds fail due to an empty `repository_name` variable.

**The problem being solved:**
Currently, the `tpu_docker_images_pipeline.yml` and `gpu_docker_images_pipeline.yml` workflows define `repository_name` as a `workflow_dispatch` input. However, GitHub Actions does not populate the `inputs` context for scheduled runs. When the pipeline calls the reusable `build_and_push_docker_image.yml` workflow during a nightly run, the `${{ inputs.repository_name }}` evaluates to an empty string.

This results in a double slash (`//`) in the Docker image tag path, causing the `build-push-action` step to fail with the following error:
`invalid tag "us-docker.pkg.dev/tpu-prod-env-multipod//maxtext_jax_stable:...": invalid reference format`

**Why this is a good solution:**
By adding a logical OR fallback (`${{ inputs.repository_name || 'maxtext-images' }}`), we ensure that the default `maxtext-images` repository name is always populated during scheduled runs, while still allowing users to override it when triggering a manual `workflow_dispatch`.

# Tests

- CI checks will verify the YAML syntax. 
- Fully verifying this requires the next scheduled cron run to trigger.

title: feat(models): add qwen3.5-35b-a3b-fp8 and qwen3.5-397b-a17b-fp8 model configs and HuggingFace mapping
body:
# Description

Adds FP8 weight-only model configurations, dynamic dequantization layer wiring, and Hugging Face checkpoint conversion mappings for **Qwen 3.5 35B** (`Qwen/Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-FP8`) and **Qwen 3.5 397B** (`Qwen/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-FP8`).

> [!NOTE]
> The 35B variant is validated end-to-end (checkpoint conversion, forward logit parity, autoregressive decoding, and distributed training). The **397B variant is config-only**: it shares the identical architecture family, parameter mapping, and dynamic dequantization engine, and is validated via `configs_test.py` smoke tests, but has **not** been validated end-to-end at scale on hardware. Reviewers should treat 397B as an enablement configuration.

### Summary of Changes:
1. **Model Configurations (`src/maxtext/configs/models/`)**:
   - Added `qwen3.5-35b-a3b-fp8.yml` and `qwen3.5-397b-a17b-fp8.yml` configuring FP8 weight-only storage (`weight_dtype: "float8_e4m3fn"`, `weight_block_size: 128`, compute `dtype: "bfloat16"`).
   - Set `float32_gate_logits: True` for numerical stability in MoE routing.
   - Declaratively specified `unquantized_modules` matching official Hugging Face quantization configs to preserve high-precision (`bfloat16`) for embeddings, norms, routing gates (`gate`, `shared_expert_gate`), and linear attention projections (`conv1d`, `in_proj_ba`, `A_log`, `dt_bias`).
   - Both configs inherit `sparse_matmul: True` from `base.yml` (Megablox sparse matmul) for production training and inference.
2. **Model Definition & Dequantization Wiring (`src/maxtext/models/qwen3.py`, `qwen3_5.py`)**:
   - Passed `weight_block_size` to linear attention projections (`in_proj_qkvz`, `out_proj`) in `Qwen3NextGatedDeltaNet` to enable block-scaled dequantization.
   - Wired `get_weight_dtype(cfg, ...)` across `Qwen3NextGatedDeltaNet`, `Qwen3NextSparseMoeBlock`, and `Qwen3_5DecoderLayer` to respect `unquantized_modules`.
   - Updated weight initialization (`conv_kernel_init` and `a_log_init`) to sample in `float32` when target dtypes are sub-byte / FP8 types, preventing truncation or numerical instability during initialization.
3. **Precision & Normalization Fixes (`src/maxtext/layers/normalizations.py`)**:
   - Updated `Qwen3NextRMSNorm` to compute `(1.0 + scale)` in `float32` prior to casting to `bfloat16`, eliminating mantissa truncation on small scale offsets ($\sim 10^{-3}$).
4. **Parameter Mapping & 2D Block Scale Hooks (`src/maxtext/checkpoint_conversion/utils/param_mapping.py`)**:
   - Extended `QWEN3_5_MAXTEXT_TO_HF_PARAM_MAPPING` to map companion `kernel_scale` parameters for self-attention (Q, K, V, Out), linear attention (`in_proj_qkvz`, `out_proj`), MLP shared expert, and MoE routed experts across scanned and unscanned modes.
   - Added 2D block scale transposition and composite scale hook functions (`reshape_scale`, `split_qkvz_scale`, `split_ba_scale`, and `process_wi_0_wi_1_scale`) to properly split and concatenate compound scale tensors.
   - Registered `qwen3.5-35b-a3b-fp8`, `qwen3.5-35b-fp8`, and `qwen3.5-397b-a17b-fp8` in `PARAM_MAPPING` and `HOOK_FNS`.
5. **Hugging Face Model Registry & Types**:
   - Registered FP8 model identifiers in `HF_IDS` (`src/maxtext/utils/globals.py`), `HF_MODEL_CONFIGS`, `HF_SHAPE` (`src/maxtext/checkpoint_conversion/utils/`), `_MODEL_TO_BLOCKS` (`src/maxtext/multimodal/processor.py`), `src/maxtext/layers/nnx_decoders.py`, and `ModelName` (`src/maxtext/configs/types.py`).
6. **Unit Tests & Test Registries**:
   - Registered `qwen3.5-35b-a3b.yml`, `qwen3.5-35b-a3b-fp8.yml`, and `qwen3.5-397b-a17b-fp8.yml` in `tests/unit/configs_test.py` (`QWEN_CONFIGS`).

# Tests

### Unit Tests
- Unit tests for all Qwen model configurations:
  ```bash
  PYTHONPATH=src pytest tests/unit/configs_test.py -k "qwen" -v
  ```
  Result: 14 passed, 0 failed.
- Full configuration suite:
  ```bash
  PYTHONPATH=src pytest tests/unit/configs_test.py -v
  ```
  Result: 79 passed, 0 failed.
- Pyconfig test suite:
  ```bash
  PYTHONPATH=src pytest tests/unit/pyconfig_test.py -v
  ```
  Result: 29 passed, 0 failed.

### End-to-End Validation (Qwen 3.5 35B FP8)
- **Forward Pass Logit Parity vs Hugging Face Golden** ([Run Log](https://paste.googleplex.com/4561960650276864)):
  - Validated on TPU v4-8 against official Hugging Face reference outputs (`tests/utils/forward_pass_logit_checker.py`).
  - Achieved **max KL divergence of 0.00143** (well below the `< 0.01` parity threshold and `< 0.2` assertion limit), with **10/10 top-token overlap** and **1.0 Jaccard similarity**.
  - *Note on `sparse_matmul`*: The test harness explicitly sets `sparse_matmul=false` to use the dense reference MoE path during parity evaluation, bypassing Megablox sparse matmul numerical divergence (documented in `qwen3_next_vs_reference_test.py:L670-672`) to strictly isolate FP8 dequantization parity.
- **Autoregressive Decoding Verification** ([Run Log](https://paste.googleplex.com/6526063589588992)):
  - Executed on TPU v4-8 with exit code 0.
  - Successfully generated 63 tokens at **~4.3 tok/s (234.9 ms/step)** with coherent, fluent text generation on standard attention benchmark prompts.
- **Distributed Training Verification** ([Run Log](https://paste.googleplex.com/5924369256284160)):
  - Executed 10 training steps (steps 0–9) on a **TPU v5p-128 slice (64 chips, FSDP=16, EP=4)** with exit code 0 using the `c4` dataset, dequantizing from the FP8 checkpoint on load.
  - Demonstrated stable loss progression (**`lm_loss: 2.725`** at step 9) and verified asynchronous Orbax checkpoint saving at step 9.

title: Onboard Qwen3.5 397b fp8
body:
# Description

Onboards `Qwen/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-FP8` to MaxText and fixes scale-tensor sharding for block-scaled FP8 modules:

1. **Qwen3.5-397B-FP8 Model Onboarding**:
   - Adds `qwen3.5-397b-a17b-fp8.yml` configuring FP8 weight storage (`weight_dtype: "float8_e4m3fn"`), 128x128 block scaling (`weight_block_size: 128`), and full-precision preservation for `unquantized_modules`.
   - Registers the model across HuggingFace checkpoint conversion and metadata mappings (`hf_model_configs.py`, `hf_shape.py`, `param_mapping.py`, `globals.py`, `types.py`).

2. **Block Scale Sharding Fixes**:
   - **`DenseGeneral`**: Replicates block-compressed scale dimensions instead of inheriting the kernel's mesh axes. Inheriting kernel sharding causes divisibility crashes when FSDP/TP mesh degree exceeds the compressed dimension (e.g., FSDP > 32 on a 32-block axis).
   - **`RoutedMoE`**: Shards expert scales strictly along the expert axis (`wi_kernel_axes[0]`) and replicates the block-tile dimensions.
   - Updates `tests/unit/linears_test.py` to assert scale replication on block-tiled layers.

# Tests

* `JAX_PLATFORMS=cpu PYTHONPATH=src pytest tests/unit/configs_test.py tests/unit/pyconfig_test.py -q`
* `JAX_PLATFORMS=cpu PYTHONPATH=src pytest tests/unit/linears_test.py -q`

The 2.13 ROCm wheel appears to rely on something present in the ROCm builder image to detect the CPU vectorized ISA, so it works when run on a ROCm image but fails on a plain CPU-only image.

Workaround: run the +rocm wheel on a ROCm image, or install a standard CPU/CUDA build for GPU-less environments.

Updates `transformers` from 4.31.0 to 5.5.0
Release notes

Sourced from transformers's releases.

Release v5.5.0

New Model additions

Gemma4

Gemma 4 is a multimodal model with pretrained and instruction-tuned variants, available in 1B, 13B, and 27B parameters. The architecture is mostly the same as the previous Gemma versions. The key differences are a vision processor that can output images of fixed token budget and a spatial 2D RoPE to encode vision-specific information across height and width axis.

You can find all the original Gemma 4 checkpoints under the Gemma 4 release.

The key difference from previous Gemma releases is the new design to process images of different sizes using a fixed-budget number of tokens. Unlike many models that squash every image into a fixed square (like 224×224), Gemma 4 keeps the image's natural aspect ratio while making it the right size. There a a couple constraints to follow:

  • The total number of pixels must fit within a patch budget
  • Both height and width must be divisible by 48 (= patch size 16 × pooling kernel 3)

[!IMPORTANT] Gemma 4 does not apply the standard ImageNet mean/std normalization that many other vision models use. The model's own patch embedding layer handles the final scaling internally (shifting values to the [-1, 1] range).

The number of "soft tokens" (aka vision tokens) an image processor can produce is configurable. The supported options are outlined below and the default is 280 soft tokens per image.

Soft Tokens Patches (before pooling) Approx. Image Area
70 630 ~161K pixels
140 1,260 ~323K pixels
280 2,520 ~645K pixels
560 5,040 ~1.3M pixels
1,120 10,080 ~2.6M pixels

To encode positional information for each patch in the image, Gemma 4 uses a learned 2D position embedding table. The position table stores up to 10,240 positions per axis, which allows the model to handle very large images. Each position is a learned vector of the same dimensions as the patch embedding. The 2D RoPE which Gemma 4 uses independently rotate half the attention head dimensions for the x-axis and the other half for the y-axis. This allows the model to understand spatial relationships like "above," "below," "left of," and "right of."

NomicBERT

NomicBERT is a BERT-inspired encoder model that applies Rotary Position Embeddings (RoPE) to create reproducible long context text embeddings. It is the first fully reproducible, open-source text embedding model with 8192 context length that outperforms both OpenAI Ada-002 and OpenAI text-embedding-3-small on short-context MTEB and long context LoCo benchmarks. The model generates dense vector embeddings for various tasks including search, clustering, and classification using specific instruction prefixes.

Links: Documentation | Paper

  • Internalise the NomicBERT model (#43067) by @​ed22699 in #43067

MusicFlamingo

Music Flamingo is a fully open large audio–language model designed for robust understanding and reasoning over music. It builds upon the Audio Flamingo 3 architecture by including Rotary Time Embeddings (RoTE), which injects temporal position information to enable the model to handle audio sequences up to 20 minutes. The model features a unified audio encoder across speech, sound, and music with special sound boundary tokens for improved audio sequence modeling.

12. Delete Linen-specific code paths and NNX compatibility flags — delivered as 5 stacked PRs (12.1–12.5):
    12.1. 🔄 **[This PR]** Collapse Linen dispatch in core utils / quantization / checkpointing / sharding (`maxtext_utils`, `train_utils`, `sharding`, `model_creation_utils`, checkpoint scripts, `layers/quantizations`) + their unit tests. Pure dead-branch removal — the three flags still exist, so no config change. Base `main`. (PR #4357)
    12.2. ❌ Collapse Linen dispatch in trainers (pre-train, DiLoCo, GRPO); regenerate the NNX DPO golden.
    12.3. ❌ Collapse Linen dispatch in inference (maxengine, kvcache, vLLM, LoRA).
    12.4. ❌ Delete the Linen decoder/attention/embedding layers + `*_as_linen` model wrappers.
    12.5. ❌ Remove the `pure_nnx` / `enable_nnx` / `pure_nnx_decoder` config flags.

# Description

First of five stacked PRs that finish the Flax Linen → NNX migration by deleting the Linen code paths. Now that PR #3526 flipped the NNX defaults to `True`, every `if config.pure_nnx: … else: <linen>` branch is dead code, so this series removes it one subsystem at a time, then deletes the Linen classes, then drops the flags.

This one handles the core utilities. It removes the Linen branch of every `pure_nnx` / `enable_nnx` / `pure_nnx_decoder` / `isinstance(model, nn.Module)` conditional in the abstract-state and model creation helpers, checkpointing, sharding, quantization, muon, and the standalone checkpoint scripts, and updates the matching unit tests to drop the now-dead Linen cases. It's pure dead-branch removal — with the NNX defaults those branches never ran — and the three flags still exist (they come out in 5/5), so nothing about the config surface changes here.

title: Feature/sft windowing
body:
# Description

Completion-only SFT (grain pipeline) currently **head-truncates** any example longer
than `max_target_length`: `SFTPromptMasking` concatenates the prompt/completion into
`inputs`/`targets` and slices `[:max_target_length]`. For any over-length example this
drops the tail — **including the turn terminator `<end_of_turn>`** — from both `inputs`
and `targets`. The stop token therefore never enters the loss for long examples, and the
model is trained on a stop-less completion prefix, which teaches it to keep generating
and not stop on long outputs (observed as long-generation repetition after SFT).

This PR adds an **opt-in** long-example handling mode, `sft_long_example_handling='window'`,
implemented as `SFTPromptMaskingWindows` — a one-to-many `FlatMapTransform`. Instead of
truncating, an over-length example is split into multiple `<= max_target_length` records
via a prompt-pinned sliding window:

- the conversation-prefix-so-far is replayed (front-capped) as **masked** context in front
  of each window,
- a small **masked** completion overlap gives local continuity across the split,
- the new completion tokens are tiled across windows with **disjoint loss** — every
  completion token is trained exactly once,
- the **final window retains `<end_of_turn>`**, so the terminator always enters the loss.

Examples that already fit within `max_target_length` yield a single record byte-identical
to `SFTPromptMasking`. The default stays `'truncate'`, so behavior is unchanged unless the
new mode is explicitly enabled — **fully backward compatible**.

Why windowing rather than simply dropping over-length examples: dropping discards training
signal and biases the dataset toward short conversations; windowing keeps every completion
token (including the terminator) in the loss while still respecting `max_target_length`, at
the cost of a bounded per-example fan-out.

**Config knobs** (all with backward-compatible defaults):
- `sft_long_example_handling: 'truncate' | 'window'` — default `'truncate'`
- `sft_window_overlap` — default `256`; masked completion carryover between consecutive
  windows (clamped to `<= max_target_length // 8`)
- `sft_window_context_cap` — default `-1` (auto = `max_target_length // 2`); max masked
  conversation-prefix context pinned in front of each window
- `sft_window_max_fan_out` — default `32`; hard cap on records emitted per example
  (runaway guard; excess trailing tokens are dropped and logged)

`'window'` requires `sft_train_on_completion_only=True` (context/overlap tokens are masked
with `unk_id`).

**Implementation:**
- `input_pipeline/input_pipeline_utils.py`: new `SFTPromptMaskingWindows` transform +

title: Fix multiprocess dataloader CPU iteration leak via weakref sweep
body:
## Overview & Motivation

Resolves [b/532239140](https://b.corp.google.com/issues/532239140): *[Pathways Elasticity/RemoteIterator] Slice scale up using Grain Colocated Data Loading on v6e cluster creates large step times (200s+)*

In elastic training workloads on Google Cloud TPU (e.g. v6e clusters using Multi-Tier Checkpointing / Pathways elasticity), cluster preemption or worker disruption causes the framework to gracefully scale down (e.g. from 2 slices to 1 slice) and subsequently scale back up once the interrupted slice recovers.

When using **Grain with Colocated Python Data Loading** (`colocated_python_data_input=True` and `grain_worker_count > 0`), workloads experienced severe, permanent performance degradation immediately following slice scale-up:
- Healthy step times before interruption: **~1.85s / step** (~4,400 Tokens/s/device).
- Post-scale-up step times: degraded exponentially to **60s – 120s+ (and up to 200s+)**, eventually triggering timeout or hang detection.

---

## Root Cause Analysis

Grain data loading executes inside the companion **`colocated-python-sidecar`** container running alongside the TPU worker pod. 

1. **Process Reparenting to PID 1**: When a worker pod or Pathways process crashes and recovers, `main.py` inside the sidecar is restarted by the container entrypoint loop (`while true; do python /app/main.py; done`).
2. **Zombie / Orphaned Multiprocessing Workers**: While `main.py` restarts, its previous child worker processes (`multiprocessing.spawn` and `resource_tracker`) are **not** reaped by `/bin/sh`. The Linux kernel reparents them to **`PID 1`**.
3. **Hidden from Python GC**: Because these orphaned processes no longer exist in the new Python process’s `multiprocessing.process._children`, standard Python cleanup (`multiprocessing.active_children()`) cannot detect or terminate them.
4. **GCS Contention & Data Starvation**: The orphaned workers remain permanently alive in the background holding open thousands of file descriptors and TCP streams to Google Cloud Storage array-record chunks. When the new `main.py` spawns fresh workers upon scale-up, they contend with the zombie processes for bandwidth and lock files, causing `ExternalSidecar::Execute` batch fetching to block for 60s–120s per step.

---

## Proposed Changes

1. **Direct `/proc` Orphan Process Cleanup (`multihost_dataloading.py`)**:
   - Added `_cleanup_orphaned_multiprocessing_processes(force_all=False)`: Directly scans `/proc` for any `multiprocessing.spawn` or `multiprocessing.resource_tracker` processes whose parent process (`PPid`) is `1` (or dead) and terminates them via `SIGTERM` followed by `SIGKILL`.
   - Called during `RemoteIterator.__init__()` prior to `self.reset()`, and on `RemoteIterator.close()` and `MultiHostDataLoadIterator.close()`.

2. **Singleton Object Store & Global Iterator Purge**:
   - Explicitly sweeps `SINGLETON_OBJECT_STORE._storage` on worker nodes during iterator re-initialization to ensure stale `RemoteIterator` instances do not linger in memory.
   - Added `cleanup_all_iterators()` using `weakref.WeakSet` to track and force `.close()` on any active iterators across the process.

3. **Elastic Resilience Hooks (`elastic_utils.py`)**:
   - Integrated `cleanup_all_iterators()` into `maybe_elastic_scale_up()` prior to raising `ScaleUpSignalError()`.
   - Integrated `cleanup_all_iterators()` into `cleanup_iterators_and_checkpoints()` as the default `on_elastic_event_callback` for `elastic_retry()`.

---

## Empirical Verification

Tested on cluster `bodaborg-v6e-256-lcscld-c` (`southamerica-west1-a`, project `tpu-prod-env-one-vm`) with Llama 3.1 8B on 2 slices of TPU v6e:

1. **Initial 2-Slice Baseline (Steps 0–6)**:
   - Stable step duration: **1.860s – 1.865s** (~4,410 Tokens/s/device).
2. **Fault Injection & 1-Slice Degradation (Steps 0–38)**:
   - Injected `SIGILL` into `worker-0-0` at step 4+. Pathways smoothly degraded to 1 slice (16 devices) at **~1.87s/step**.
3. **Scale-Up to 2 Slices & Defect Reproduction (Steps 27–31)**:
   - Pathways re-established 2 slices.
   - Without orphan cleanup, step times immediately stalled at **85.96s (Step 27)**, **123.20s (Step 28)**, **66.48s (Step 29)**, and **120.82s (Step 30)** due to orphaned PIDs 4716 and 4718.
4. **Post-Cleanup Recovery & Steady State (Steps 32–1000)**:
   - Upon invoking `_cleanup_orphaned_multiprocessing_processes()`, orphaned processes were terminated.
   - Step times collapsed immediately from **123.2s $\to$ 1.848s – 1.95s/step** (~4,420 Tokens/s/device).
   - Training ran cleanly and steadily all the way to **step 1,000** without further degradation or `DATA_LOSS` errors.
5. **Raw Log Verification (Internal GCP Links)**
    - Patched Execution (Stable 2.0s post-recovery):** [Job Logs](https://cloudlogging.app.goo.gl/FA2KsPUuz1PZimV59)

---

## Operational Deployment Note

Because JAX `colocated_python.colocated_python_class(RemoteIterator)` serializes classes by global module reference (`('maxtext.input_pipeline.multihost_dataloading', 'RemoteIterator')`), the companion `colocated-python-sidecar` container resolves and imports this code from its own container filesystem (`/app/maxtext`).

**Action Item upon Merge**: The companion container image (`us-docker.pkg.dev/.../sidecar_mtc`) will need to be rebuilt and released from `main` so that the running sidecars incorporate these changes.

title: feat(checkpointing): add dequantize-on-load parameter restoration
body:
# Description

Upgrades `src/maxtext/common/checkpointing.py` to support restoring FP8 Orbax checkpoints and introduces **automatic in-memory dequantize-on-load** with **dynamic companion scale sharding derivation for multi-host distributed restoration under Orbax v1**.

### Motivation & Context
Full pre-training and fine-tuning with optimizers like AdamW require unquantized BF16 master weights, as optimizer states and gradient accumulation are not supported on raw 8-bit floats. This feature enables loading a quantized FP8 checkpoint directly into an unquantized model (`weight_dtype="bfloat16"`), saving ~50% disk storage and transfer bandwidth while automatically reconstructing `bfloat16` weights in memory upon restore without requiring an offline conversion step.

### How to Use Dequantize-on-Load
To use dequantize-on-load, specify the **unquantized** model name (or set `weight_dtype=bfloat16`), but point `load_parameters_path` directly at an **FP8 quantized Orbax checkpoint**:

```bash
# Example: Restore an FP8 checkpoint into an unquantized BF16 model for decode / eval:
python3 -m maxtext.inference.decode \
  src/maxtext/configs/base.yml \
  model_name=qwen3.5-35b-a3b \
  load_parameters_path=/path/to/fp8_checkpoint/0/items \
  per_device_batch_size=1

# Example: Restore an FP8 checkpoint into an unquantized BF16 model for fine-tuning / training:
python3 -m maxtext.trainers.pre_train.train \
  src/maxtext/configs/base.yml \
  model_name=qwen3.5-35b-a3b \
  load_parameters_path=/path/to/fp8_checkpoint/0/items
```

**What happens:**
1. MaxText instantiates the model architecture in memory using `bfloat16` (the target abstract schema `want` expects BF16 weights and no scale parameters).
2. `load_params_from_path` inspects checkpoint metadata, discovers companion scale tensors (`kernel_scale`, `wi_0_scale`, etc.), and temporarily augments the restore schema to retrieve both the FP8 weights and companion scales from disk.
3. For multi-host distributed restore, `_scale_sharding` derives partition specs for companion scale tensors from their parent weights, ensuring every host owns addressable shards.
4. Restored FP8 weights are dynamically dequantized in memory to `bfloat16` using `quantizations.dequantize_weight`, and companion scale tensors are dropped.
5. The model receives pure `bfloat16` weights and runs without any runtime quantization overhead.

### Key Changes
1. **Target State Augmentation (`_augment_want_with_scales` & `_augment_target_with_scales`):**
   - Discovers companion scale tensors (`{weight}_scale`) present in checkpoint metadata but omitted from the unquantized target model (`want`).
   - Augments the target abstract schema (`ShapeDtypeStruct`) so Orbax restores both the weights and their scale parameters without schema mismatches.
   - Supports both Flax NNX models (`nnx.replace_by_pure_dict`) and Linen nested / flat dictionary checkpoint layouts.
2. **Companion Scale Sharding Derivation (`_scale_sharding`):**
   - Under Orbax v1, the abstract target tree is consumed directly without normalization. Leaving sharding unspecified on injected scale leaves causes non-primary hosts to have no addressable shards, crashing in `jax.make_array_from_single_device_arrays`.
   - `_scale_sharding` dynamically derives companion scale `NamedSharding` from the underlying weight sharding:
     - For blockwise scales, retains dividing mesh axes via `maxtext_sharding.adjust_pspec_for_indivisible_shapes(spec, scale_shape, mesh)` and replicates the rest.
     - For per-tensor scalar scales (rank 0) or rank mismatches (1D per-channel scales), falls back to replicated `NamedSharding(mesh, PartitionSpec())`.
     - Defensively guarded with a `try...except Exception` fallback to replicated `P()`.
3. **In-Memory Dequantization (`maybe_dequantize_restored_params`):**
   - Single-pass traversal over restored parameters: when a weight and its companion scale are present but the target model expects an unquantized weight, dequantizes the weight to the target dtype using `quantizations.dequantize_weight` and strips the companion scale.
   - Supports scalar, 1D per-channel, 2D blockwise, and 3D MoE (blockwise and per-expert) scaling topologies.
   - Preserves unquantized companion parameters (e.g. `bias`) intact.
4. **Pre-load Architectural Validation:**
   - Compares checkpoint metadata against the target model before loading, raising a descriptive `ValueError` on shape mismatches rather than failing mid-restore.
5. **Direct FP8 Loading Preserved:**
   - If the target model expects `weight_dtype="float8_e4m3fn"` (e.g. `model_name=qwen3.5-35b-a3b-fp8`), weights and scales are loaded directly without dequantization.

Part 3 in the FP8 Weight-Only Dynamic Dequantization series (depends on #5053, #5052).

# Tests

### 1. Unit Tests (`tests/unit/checkpointing_test.py`)
Ran all 10 unit tests in `FP8DequantizeOnLoadTest` covering NNX, Linen, various scale topologies, and multi-axis scale sharding:
```bash
PYTHONPATH=src JAX_PLATFORMS=cpu pytest tests/unit/checkpointing_test.py -k "FP8DequantizeOnLoadTest" -v
```
**Result:** `10 passed, 0 failures` (full test suite: 30 passed).

- `test_load_fp8_checkpoint_into_bf16_nnx_model`: Verifies NNX dequantize-on-load to BF16, scale removal, and unquantized `bias` preservation.
- `test_load_fp8_checkpoint_into_fp8_nnx_model`: Verifies direct FP8 restoration preserves weights and scale tensors.
- `test_load_fp8_checkpoint_into_bf16_linen_dict`: Verifies legacy Linen dictionary layout dequantization.
- `test_load_fp8_checkpoint_with_per_channel_scale_into_bf16_model`: Verifies 1D per-channel scale dequantization on load.
- `test_load_fp8_checkpoint_with_blockwise_scales_into_bf16_model`: Verifies 2D blockwise scale dequantization on load.
- `test_load_fp8_checkpoint_with_moe_scales_into_bf16_model`: Verifies 3D blockwise and per-expert MoE scale dequantization with asymmetric tensors.
- `test_load_fp8_checkpoint_shape_mismatch_raises`: Verifies pre-load shape mismatch detection with informative error messaging.
- `test_augment_want_with_scales_flat_linen_checkpoint`: Verifies schema augmentation on flat Linen / SFT checkpoints.
- `test_load_fp8_flat_linen_checkpoint`: Mock-based integration test exercising the flat Linen checkpoint restore flow.
- `test_scale_sharding_derivation`: Verifies `_scale_sharding` across 5 mesh topologies (unsharded/None, divisible block scale, scalar rank-0 replication, 1D per-channel replication, and 4D MoE block scale with leading unpartitioned dimensions).

### 2. Multi-Host Distributed Restore Verification (TPU v5p-128 / 16-host)
- Tested distributed restore on a 16-host, 128-chip TPU cluster (`v5p-128`) on GKE via XPK (cluster `bodaborg-v5p-nap`, project `cloud-tpu-shared-capacity`).
- Restored an FP8 Qwen 3.5 35B checkpoint into an unquantized BF16 training state (`model_name=qwen3.5-35b-a3b`, `load_parameters_path=gs://snehalv-data/qwen35local/scanned/0`) with FSDP and EP partitioned across 16 hosts.
- Verified that `_scale_sharding` resolves the Orbax v1 `ValueError: If the Array has no addressable shards` failure by properly providing addressable device shardings for all companion scales across all 16 hosts.

### 3. Single-Host Hardware Verification (Remote TPU v4-8 VM)
- **Forward-Pass Logit Parity (`tests/utils/run_fp8_logit_test.py`):** Verified against Hugging Face golden logits on TPU v4-8 (`EXIT_CODE=0`, max KL divergence < 0.007 across prompts vs. 0.2 threshold, 29/30 top-10 token match).
- **Greedy Autoregressive Decode (`tests/utils/run_fp8_decode_test.py`):** Verified end-to-end token generation on TPU v4-8 (`EXIT_CODE=0`, 239 ms/tok steady-state latency, 8.32 GiB HBM post-load).

### 4. Code Hygiene & Formatting
- Linters passed cleanly: `codespell`, `pylint` (zero warnings on modified code), `pyink`.

title: CI: fix empty repository_name breaking all scheduled Docker image builds
body:
# Description

All scheduled nightly TPU and GPU Docker image builds have been failing since `f31eb78a` ("Migrate MaxText Docker images to Artifact Registry"). This PR fixes the root cause and adds a fail-fast guard so the same class of bug surfaces in seconds instead of after a multi-minute image build.

## Root cause

The `inputs` context is **empty on `schedule` events** — `workflow_dispatch` input defaults are not applied to scheduled runs. So `${{ inputs.repository_name }}` resolved to an empty string in both nightly pipelines.

Before the migration the tag was `gcr.io/${{ vars.PROJECT_NAME }}/${{ inputs.image_name }}`, which had no repository segment, so nothing depended on `repository_name`. The migration changed it to the four-segment Artifact Registry path `us-docker.pkg.dev/${{ vars.PROJECT_NAME }}/${{ inputs.repository_name }}/${{ inputs.image_name }}`, and the empty value became a blank path segment:

```
[command]/usr/local/bin/docker buildx build ... --tag us-docker.pkg.dev/tpu-prod-env-multipod//maxtext_gpu_jax_nightly:35041297571 ...
ERROR: failed to build: invalid tag "us-docker.pkg.dev/tpu-prod-env-multipod//maxtext_gpu_jax_nightly:35041297571": invalid reference format
```

Note that the TPU pipeline already declares `default: "maxtext-images"` on the dispatch input and still failed, which confirms the default is not honored on `schedule`.

The failure also went unreported: the `notify_failure` job is guarded by `inputs.repository_name == 'maxtext-images'`, which is false on scheduled runs for exactly the same reason, so no issue was ever filed.

Affected runs (both from the 2026-09-16 00:00 UTC cron):

| Pipeline | Run | Failure |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| GPU Docker Images Pipeline | [35041297571](https://github.com/AI-Hypercomputer/maxtext/actions/runs/35041297571) | 2/2 build jobs, `.../multipod//maxtext_gpu_jax_nightly` |
| TPU Docker Images Pipeline | [35041264238](https://github.com/AI-Hypercomputer/maxtext/actions/runs/35041264238) | 4/4 build jobs, `.../multipod//maxtext_jax_nightly` |

The surfaced annotation "Executing the custom container implementation failed. Please contact your self hosted runner administrator." is downstream noise, not a runner/infra problem.

## Changes

1. **`tpu_docker_images_pipeline.yml` / `gpu_docker_images_pipeline.yml`** — use `${{ inputs.repository_name || 'maxtext-images' }}` at every use site: the `build_and_push_docker_image.yml` call, the `run_ci_tests.yml` call, and the `notify_failure` guard. The `run_ci_tests` call needs the same fallback so it resolves the identical image path the build job pushed to.
2. **`gpu_docker_images_pipeline.yml`** — the dispatch input was `required: true` with no default, unlike the TPU pipeline. Changed to `required: false` with `default: "maxtext-images"` so the two pipelines behave the same.
3. **`build_and_push_docker_image.yml`** — new `Validate image tag components` step in the existing `pre_build_check` job. It asserts `vars.PROJECT_NAME`, `inputs.repository_name`, and `inputs.image_name` are all non-empty, echoes the resolved image path, and fails with `::error::Empty image tag component(s): ...` otherwise. `pre_build_check` runs on `ubuntu-latest` in ~2s and already gates the expensive build, so this is the cheapest possible place to catch it.

### Why a literal fallback rather than a shared default

`jobs.<id>.with` only accepts the `github`, `needs`, `strategy`, `matrix`, `inputs`, and `vars` contexts — `env` is not available there, so a workflow-level `env: DEFAULT_REPOSITORY_NAME` cannot be referenced from the reusable-workflow call. A repository variable (`vars.DOCKER_REPOSITORY_NAME`) would work and would remove the repeated literal; happy to switch to that if a maintainer sets the variable, but I did not want this fix to depend on a repo settings change.

# Tests

**1. `actionlint` (+ `shellcheck`) and `yamllint`**, matching the versions and args pinned in `.pre-commit-config.yaml`:

```bash
actionlint -ignore 'label ".*" is unknown' \
  .github/workflows/gpu_docker_images_pipeline.yml \
  .github/workflows/tpu_docker_images_pipeline.yml \
  .github/workflows/build_and_push_docker_image.yml
# exit 0

yamllint .github/workflows/gpu_docker_images_pipeline.yml \
         .github/workflows/tpu_docker_images_pipeline.yml \
         .github/workflows/build_and_push_docker_image.yml
# exit 0
```

**2. Functional test of the new guard script**, including the exact state of the failing nightly run:

```
PASS [empty repository_name (regression)] exit=1 :: ::error::Empty image tag component(s): inputs.repository_name
PASS [empty project]                      exit=1 :: ::error::Empty image tag component(s): vars.PROJECT_NAME
PASS [empty image]                        exit=1 :: ::error::Empty image tag component(s): inputs.image_name
PASS [all empty]                          exit=1 :: ::error::Empty image tag component(s): vars.PROJECT_NAME inputs.repository_name inputs.image_name
PASS [all populated (happy path)]         exit=0 :: Image tag: us-docker.pkg.dev/tpu-prod-env-multipod/maxtext-images/maxtext_gpu_jax_nightly
```

**3. Not yet verified:** an actual end-to-end scheduled run. The `schedule` trigger only fires on `main`, so this cannot be reproduced from a fork or a PR branch. A maintainer can confirm on merge by checking that the next 00:00 UTC run tags `us-docker.pkg.dev/<project>/maxtext-images/maxtext_jax_nightly:<run_id>` with no double slash. A `workflow_dispatch` run of either pipeline with `repository_name` left blank also exercises the fallback path.

title: fix(gcs_utils): spurious PermissionError on GCS paths without TensorFlow
body:
## Description

Every checkpoint save to a GCS path fails with a misleading permission error, even when the path is fully writable:                                                                                     
                                                                                                                              
                                                                                                                              
`PermissionError: Failed to create the directory 'gs://.../to_maxtext/unscanned/...'. Please check that you have write access.  `                                             
                                                                                                                              
This broke all checkpoint conversion / training runs that write to GCS once tensorflow became optional (#5086).

[DAG Error Log](https://efdb2a1d6c2c435b8b7de77690c286a9-dot-us-central1.composer.googleusercontent.com/dags/maxtext_e2e_tpu_checkpoint_conversion/grid?search=maxtext_e2e_tpu_checkpoint_conversion&tab=logs&tags=orbax&dag_run_id=auto_gha__34914535963__2026-09-15T00%3A55%3A18Z__checkpoint_conversion&task_id=gemma3-4b.to-mt-v5p-8.run_model.wait_for_workload_completion)

## Root Cause

`mkdir_and_check_permissions` validated directory creation with `exists()` immediately after `mkdir()`. On GCS that check silently depended on TensorFlow being installed, because `etils.epath` picks its backend based on whether `tensorflow` is importable.                                                                                    

So removing tensorflow flipped the backend and made the check fail for every GCS path, regardless of actual permissions.                                                                               
                                                                                                                              
The check was also redundant from the start: the write test directly below it is the authoritative permission check, and it never even ran because `exists()` raised first — meaning genuine permission failures were being masked too.

## Solution

Limit the `exists()` check to local paths and let the existing write test be the permission check for GCS.                                                                                             
                                                                                                                              
- `gcs_utils.py`: one-line condition change plus a comment explaining the backend difference.                                                                                                     
- `gcs_utils_test.py`: update the GCS test to assert `exists()` is no longer consulted, and add regression coverage for writable and non-writable GCS paths (the latter was previously untested).                                                                             
  
No dependency on TensorFlow is reintroduced.

# Tests

Gemma3-4b `to_mt`: https://cloudlogging.app.goo.gl/nJ6YDAbSRijpAfN66

title: Shard the GatedDeltaNet sequence under ici_context_parallelism
body:
Fixes #4932.

Two pspecs pinned the GDN sequence axis to `None`, and the inter-chunk recurrence was a sequential `lax.scan`. Together they mean `ici_context_parallelism` can't shard the GDN sequence at all, so neither 256K nor 1M is reachable at any chip count.

The recurrence is affine in the state:

```
h' = (exp(g_last)·I − k_gᵀ·w)·h + k_gᵀ·u  =  A·h + B
```

Each device folds its local chunks into one `(A, B)` pair with a `lax.scan`, not `associative_scan`, which would materialize the running composition per chunk, 17 GB per device at a million tokens. The pairs then compose across devices with a Hillis-Steele prefix scan over `ppermute`: log2(D) exchanges holding one pair, O(1) in the device count. `A` and `B` are 128x128 at every published Qwen 3.5 size, so the payload doesn't grow with the model.

An all-gather composes the pairs correctly too, and that's what the first push of this PR did. It materializes `[D, B, H, K, K]` and `[D, B, H, K, V]` on every device, which is O(D) per layer: about 38 GB across the 48 GatedDeltaNet layers at `ctx=256`. That term is what made raising the context axis cost memory instead of saving it.

`qkvz_pspec` had the sequence axis hardcoded replicated, which told XLA to gather the full sequence onto every device: at `ctx=2`, seq 32,768, six live `bf16[2,32768,16,512]` buffers of 1.07 GB each. Found by diffing XLA buffer assignment between `ctx=1` and `ctx=2`.

**Measured** on Qwen3.5-27B, 256 v5p, `ctx=256`, `fsdp=1`, one 4,096-token sequence per device: **1,048,576 tokens**, loss 12.923 to 10.583. Also 524,288 on the same slice, and 131,072 on 64 chips.

## The launch flag this needs

Set `per_device_batch_size` to `1/ici_context_parallelism`. `num_target_devices` counts every mesh axis, so the local batch is `per_device_batch_size × ctx`, and the default grows it with the context axis. With the flag set, memory tracks tokens per device rather than the context degree. See #4933.

## Interaction with #4348

The two can't both be live. The fused kernel returns above the state composition, so `use_pallas` is forced false whenever a context axis is set, and sequence-sharded runs take the XLA scan. @bzantium verified that fallback is loss-preserving: 6e-6 relative on the output, 2e-5 on final state. The two are disjoint rather than stacked, so this goes against `main` and #4348 rebases on top.

## Size

`models/gdn_cp.py` is new, 113 lines. `models/qwen3.py` is +42/-4. Applies to a pristine checkout of `main` with no dependency on #4348 or on my other open PRs.

# Tests

`ici_context_parallelism=4` at sequence 32,768 and `ici_context_parallelism=8` at 262,144, both training with loss descending, on v5p and v6e. 1,048,576 tokens on 256 v5p. Memory is flat in `ctx` at a fixed local shard: about 30.5 GB on a 2,048-token shard whether `ctx` is 2 or 16, so the sizing extrapolates.

`tests/unit/gdn_cp_test.py` covers three things:

- `compose_local`, against the recurrence applied chunk by chunk in its original form. That reference never builds `A` or `B` and never calls `compose`, so it checks the affine reformulation rather than restating it. Reversing the chunk order is the negative control.
- `incoming_state` on a single-device mesh, where a shard has nothing before it.
- `incoming_state` against a sequential composition on a forced 8-device CPU mesh, over a 1-D context mesh, a 2-D fsdp x context mesh, and a tuple axis name. Breaking the chain is the negative control.

The multi-device case runs as a subprocess, so the forced device count takes effect before JAX initializes, following `tests/unit/usp_collective_test.py`. pyink clean at `--line-length=122`.

body:
# Description

Fixes two failing tests in `tests/unit/moe_test.py`.

**1. `test_moe_pin_sparse_core_with_quantize_token_all_gather_init`** — `ValidationError: When EP rank is 1, use_ring_of_experts must be False`.

The test sets `use_ring_of_experts=True` (required by `moe_quantize_token_all_gather`) but left expert parallelism at 1, which config validation rejects. Fix: `ici_expert_parallelism=4`, matching the sibling `test_moe_quantize_token_all_gather`. EP needs a multi-device mesh, so the test is marked `tpu_only` like the other EP tests here; otherwise conftest auto-marks it `cpu_only` and it runs on a single-device mesh.

**2. `test_sparse_matmul_repairs_batch_specs_only_without_expert_parallelism`** — `AttributeError: 'SimpleNamespace' object has no attribute 'moe_pin_sparse_core_all_gathers'`.

`sparse_matmul` now branches on that field, which the test's hand-built stand-in config lacks. Fix: add it with its default of `False`, keeping the test on the unpinned path it asserts on.

title: feat(checkpoint_conversion): support direct FP8 and scale tensor ingestion in to_maxtext
body:
# Description

Enhances MaxText's standalone checkpoint conversion tool (`src/maxtext/checkpoint_conversion/to_maxtext.py`) to directly ingest, serialize, and store native 8-bit float weights (`float8_e4m3fn`) and companion scale tensors into Orbax format without upcasting.

### Motivation & Context
Previously, `to_maxtext.py` only supported `save_dtype="bfloat16"` and `save_dtype="float32"`. Converting pre-quantized FP8 Hugging Face checkpoints forced CPU upcasting to BF16, doubling memory usage and storage footprint. Direct ingestion allows converting multi-gigabyte/terabyte FP8 checkpoints without memory bloat.

### Key Changes
1. **Direct PyTorch $\to$ JAX FP8 Bridging:**
   - Reinterprets PyTorch `torch.float8_e4m3fn` tensors as `uint8` views before bridging to `ml_dtypes.float8_e4m3fn` in NumPy memory, bypassing standard NumPy float8 limitations.
   - Updated `LazyHFLoader` to use `safetensors` with `framework="pt"` (when PyTorch is available) so native FP8 tensors can be deserialized from safetensors.
   - Added `ml_dtypes.float8_e4m3fn` handling to `LazyTensor` dtype initialization.
2. **Scale Key Fallback Resolution:**
   - Added `resolve_scale_key()` to resolve `.weight_scale` to `.weight_scale_inv` fallbacks in both `LazyHFLoader` and `_eager_getter`, supporting checkpoints with inverse scale naming conventions (e.g. NeuralMagic / vLLM).
3. **Source Precision Preservation:**
   - When `--save_dtype="float8_e4m3fn"`, `_convert_tensor_to_numpy` only converts FP8 weights to `ml_dtypes.float8_e4m3fn`. Companion scale tensors and unquantized modules (e.g., embeddings, norm scales, router gates) retain their source precision (BF16 or FP32).
   - In `convert_lora_to_maxtext_adapter`, adapter weights remain `bfloat16` when `save_dtype="float8_e4m3fn"`.
4. **1D Tensor Stacking & Slicing Safety (`tensor_handling.py`, `utils.py`, `to_maxtext.py`):**
   - In `_build_single_axis_stacked_tensor` (`tensor_handling.py` and `to_maxtext.py`), guarded stacking logic when `scan_layers=True`: if `len(target_shape) <= param_scan_axis` (such as 1D per-layer scalar scale tensors like Llama 3.1 FP8 `kernel_scale`), tensors are stacked along axis 0 instead of attempting an out-of-bounds stack along axis 1 (`param_scan_axis`).
   - In `process_maxtext_param` (`utils.py`), added corresponding logic to slice along axis 0 for 1D parameters during MaxText parameter export.
5. **CLI Normalization & Argument Extraction:**
   - Added `_extract_conversion_args()` and CLI argv preprocessing to allow conversion arguments (`save_dtype`, `hf_model_path`, `lazy_load_tensors`, etc.) to be supplied using standard MaxText `key=value` syntax without `--` prefixes, separating them cleanly from pyconfig arguments.
   - Expanded `--save_dtype` choices to include `float8_e4m3fn`.

Part 2 of 5 in the FP8 Weight-Only Dynamic Dequantization series (depends on #5053).

# Tests

### Automated Unit Tests
Added unit test suite in `tests/unit/to_maxtext_test.py`:
- `ResolveScaleKeyTest`: Verifies exact key matching, `.weight_scale` $\to$ `.weight_scale_inv` fallback, and unmatched key handling.
- `ConvertTensorToNumpyTest`: Verifies `torch.float8_e4m3fn` $\to$ `ml_dtypes.float8_e4m3fn` zero-copy view, FP8 $\to$ FP32 conversion, BF16 conversion, and NumPy passthrough.
- `ExtractConversionArgsTest`: Verifies extraction and separation of conversion flags from mixed pyconfig CLI arguments.

### End-to-End Verification
Tested end-to-end checkpoint conversion of Hugging Face FP8 model (`neuralmagic/Meta-Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct-FP8`):
```bash
python -m maxtext.checkpoint_conversion.to_maxtext \
  model_name=llama3.1-8b-fp8 \
  hf_model_path=neuralmagic/Meta-Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct-FP8 \
  base_output_directory=/tmp/maxtext_llama3.1_8b_fp8 \
  save_dtype=float8_e4m3fn \
  --lazy_load_tensors=True
```
Verified that linear weights are stored in `float8_e4m3fn` and scale tensors in `float32`.

title: feat(layers): implement FP8 weight-only dynamic dequantization engine and types
body:
# Description

Implements native FP8 weight-only storage with dynamic on-the-fly dequantization in MaxText's core linear and MoE layers (`DenseGeneral`, `MlpBlock`, and `RoutedMoE`).

### Motivation & Context
Open-source frontier models (e.g. Llama 3.1 8B FP8 with scalar scaling and Qwen 3.5 35B A3B FP8 with 128-block scaling) are widely distributed in quantized FP8 formats (`float8_e4m3fn` / `float8_e5m2`). Storing these checkpoints in pure BF16 requires excessive High-Bandwidth Memory (HBM), limiting rapid model bringup, inference, and logit verification on smaller TPU topologies (e.g. v4-64, v5e-8). Furthermore, TPUs prior to TPU v7 (v4, v5e, v5p) do not support native hardware FP8 matrix multiplications.

Dynamic dequantization allows weights to be stored and moved across HBM in 8-bit precision, dynamically upcasting in vector registers immediately before `lax.dot_general`, achieving a ~50% reduction in parameter memory footprint and memory-bandwidth traffic.

### Key Changes
1. **Precision Types & Configuration (`common_types.py`, `configs/types.py`, `configs/base.yml`):**
   - Registered `float8_e4m3fn` and `float8_e5m2` in the configuration schema `DType` and added `is_fp8_dtype()` helper.
   - Added `unquantized_modules` and `weight_block_size` to `Quantization` config and `base.yml`, enabling models to configure block scaling (symmetric e.g. 128x128 or asymmetric e.g. [128, 64]) and keep sensitive submodules in full precision.
   - Added `get_weight_dtype(config, module_name)` to dynamically resolve layer precision based on pattern-matched `unquantized_modules`.
2. **Quantization Configuration & Operator (`quantizations.py`):**
   - Implemented `dequantize_weight(w, scale, compute_dtype)` supporting per-tensor scalar scaling, block scaling grids (2D/3D), and general broadcastable scale shapes.
   - Added `WeightQuantConfig` dataclass and `get_weight_quant_config(config, module_name)` helper to decouple weight quantization settings from general model hyperparameters.
3. **Linear Layers & Initializers (`linears.py`, `attentions.py`, `initializers.py`):**
   - Updated `DenseGeneral` and Linen bridge `dense_general` to manage `kernel` in FP8 alongside a companion `kernel_scale` parameter, deriving partition spec shardings to match logical mesh annotations.
   - Re-exported `dequantize_weight` and `WeightQuantConfig` from `quantizations.py` for backward compatibility.
   - Updated `_compute_dot_general` / `_compute_dot_general_nnx` to dynamically upcast weights immediately before `lax.dot_general`.
   - Ensured non-FP8 weights are cast to `compute_dtype` prior to slicing and all-gather dispatch (matching unquantized AQT expectations), while keeping FP8 weights quantized until fused dequantization.
   - Added unwrapping for wrapped parameter state containers (`get_value()` / `dict`), and dequantize before slicing when `slice_bounds` is provided.
   - Wired `weight_quant` and `weight_block_size` through `Attention` projections and `MlpBlock` (`wi`, `wi_0`, `wi_1`, `wo`).
   - Updated `_default_embed_init` and `nd_dense_init` in `initializers.py` to sample distributions in `jnp.float32` and cast to target dtype when target is FP8, avoiding JAX sampling errors on 8-bit floating point dtypes.
4. **MoE Layer Support (`moe.py`):**
   - Added support for FP8 weights and companion scale parameters in `RoutedMoE` for both prefused (`wi_scale`, `wo_scale`) and unfused (`wi_0_scale`, `wi_1_scale`, `wo_scale`) layouts.
   - Supported 1D per-expert scale grids with 1D sharding `(wi_kernel_axes[0],)` to prevent rank-mismatch issues with 3D kernel axes, as well as 3D block-scaling grids inheriting full kernel axes.
   - Dynamically dequantizes expert weights during the forward pass across all execution paths (fused RPA, prefused, and unfused).
   - Routed expert gates resolve precision via `get_weight_dtype(config, "gate")` to keep routing in high precision when declared in `unquantized_modules`.
5. **Precision Isolation & Pipeline Stage Guards (`embeddings.py`, `normalizations.py`, `nnx_decoders.py`, `nnx_scan.py`):**
   - Preserved sensitive layers (token embeddings via `Embed` and untied LM heads via `logits_dense`) in `bfloat16`/`float32` when declared in `unquantized_modules`.
   - Guaranteed RMSNorm scale parameters remain in `bfloat16`/`float32`.
   - Added dimension guards (`if x.ndim > scan_axis`) in `nnx_scan.py` and `nnx_decoders.py` to prevent crashes when moving scan axes on 0D/1D parameter leaves (e.g. scales or 1D norms).

Part 1 of 5 in the FP8 Weight-Only Dynamic Dequantization series.

# Tests

Ran unit test suites covering dynamic dequantization, MoE scale initialization and execution, and decoder layer precision isolation:
```bash
pytest tests/unit/linears_test.py tests/unit/moe_test.py tests/unit/nnx_decoders_test.py -v
```

New unit tests added:
- `tests/unit/linears_test.py`:

title: fix(gcs_utils): avoid non-existent directory check on gcs paths in mkdir_and_check_permissions
body:
### Summary
In `mkdir_and_check_permissions`, after calling `path.mkdir(exist_ok=True, parents=True)`, there was an unconditional check:
```python
if not path.exists():
  raise PermissionError(f"Failed to create the directory '{path}'. Please check that you have write access.")
```

On Google Cloud Storage (`gs://`), directories do not exist as physical objects. Calling `epath.Path.mkdir` on a GCS URI does not create directory blobs, and `epath.Path.exists()` on a new GCS prefix always returns `False`. This caused all checkpoint conversions and model checkpoint savings targeting new GCS directories to unconditionally fail with `PermissionError`.

### Fix
- Only execute `if not path.exists():` for non-GCS (POSIX/local) paths.
- For GCS paths, bucket existence is validated upfront and write permission is verified via the temporary probe file (`temp_file_path = path / f".write_test_{uuid.uuid4()}"`).
- Updated unit tests in `tests/unit/gcs_utils_test.py` to verify non-existing GCS directories pass validation when writable.
- Verified with E2E checkpoint conversion on TPU v5p cluster (`bodaborg-v5p-nap`).

title: fix(rl): restore MoE `wo` in tunix's zero-pad key set
body:
## Description

The Gemma4-26B and Qwen3-30B-A3B RL e2e pipelines fail during the **initial weight sync into the vLLM rollout**, before any RL step runs, with a Tunix `ShapeMismatchError` on the MoE `wo` weight. This restores the one-key patch that makes Tunix zero-pad `wo` instead of trying to repeat it.

```                                                                                                                  
tunix.generate.utils.ShapeMismatchError: Cannot align axis 1 for                                                                       
decoder.layers_0.mlp.moe_block.MoeBlock_0.wo: src=704 -> tgt=1024 is not an                                                            
integer multiple and the key is not a recognized MoE pattern.                                                                          
```

Affected nightly tasks:                                                                                                                
- `maxtext_e2e_tpu_post_training.rl-gemma4-26b.wait_for_workload_completion`                                                           
- `maxtext_e2e_tpu_post_training.rl-qwen3-30b.wait_for_workload_completion`

[DAG Error Log](https://efdb2a1d6c2c435b8b7de77690c286a9-dot-us-central1.composer.googleusercontent.com/dags/maxtext_e2e_tpu_post_training/grid?tab=logs&task_id=gemma4-26b.rl-gemma4-26b.rl-v5p-32.run_model.wait_for_workload_completion&dag_run_id=auto_gha__34793910551__2026-09-14T00%3A56%3A48Z__post_training)

## Root Cause

`tunix.generate.utils._align_per_axis` resolves every shape mismatch down one of two branches: MoE MLP weights are **zero-padded**, everything else is **repeated** (KV-head expansion). The branch is chosen by a leaf-key lookup, and Tunix's set omits `wo` even though its own docstring lists it:


```python                                                                                                                              
# tunix/generate/utils.py (pinned a8d7058, and google/tunix main)                                                                      
_MOE_MLP_WEIGHTS = frozenset({'wi', 'wi_0', 'wi_1'})   # `wo` missing                                                                  
``` 

MaxText's own copy of that set (`integration/vllm/convert_utils.py`) is correct and includes `wo`.

Only `wo` fails: both pipelines run with `prefuse_moe_weights=true`, so the target carries a fused `wi`, and `wi` is already in Tunix's set.                                                                              
                                                                                                                                           
This is a regression. #5025 patched the key set inside `train_rl.py::_tpu_inference_compat_patches()`; #5172 (`d043c5b8e`) removed that context manager in favour of the Raiden FFI path. But RL does not use that path yet — `MaxTextTrainingEngine.prepare_weight_sync` currently has no production caller, and `train_rl.py` still syncs through `MaxTextVllmRollout` → `VllmSampler.load_checkpoint` → Tunix `transfer_state_directly`. The shim was removed one step before its replacement was wired up.

## Solution

Re-apply the patch in `maxtext_vllm_rollout.py`, at module scope. Two deliberate differences from #5025:

- **Patch Location**: Moved the patch into the module that constructs the Tunix sampler rather than relying on `train_rl.py`'s (now removed) context manager. Module-level scope is required because the initial weight sync occurs inside `MaxTextVllmRollout.__init__` via `load_checkpoint`.
- **Dynamic Key Alignment (No Hardcoded Keys)**: Instead of hardcoding keys, it unions Tunix's set with MaxText's own `convert_utils.MOE_MLP_WEIGHTS`. This ensures both stay synchronized and allows the patch to no-op automatically once upstream `google-tunix` carries the fix (or if the internal symbol is renamed, which gracefully logs a warning and skips).


# Tests

Gemma4-26b RL E2E: https://cloudlogging.app.goo.gl/ryN9cRnkrcNzWNG38

Qwen3-30b RL E2E: https://cloudlogging.app.goo.gl/rNo1dZPCPDmAGR2S6

```bash
JAX_PLATFORMS=cpu pytest tests/post_training/unit/vllm_rollout_tunix_patch_test.py -v
```

title: Gemma-4 E2B: enable image (multimodal) E2E parity — vision clipped-linears + padded-patch masking + PLE substitution (E4B vision-tower validated; E4B E2E pending)
body:
## What
Enables **Gemma-4 E2B full end-to-end image (multimodal) parity** in MaxText. E4B runs through the same
contract-gated code path and its **vision tower is validated (cosine 0.999999 vs HF)**, but **E4B full decoder
E2E parity is PENDING** (no E4B E2E fixture/converted checkpoint this cycle) — E4B is **not** claimed as
E2E-validated.

## Reference contract (pinned)
- HF Transformers **5.9.0** (`transformers/models/gemma4/modeling_gemma4.py`), semantic reference:
  `Gemma4ClippableLinear` (clamp-in -> linear -> clamp-out) + the PLE block.
- Model/processor/tokenizer: gemma4-e2b -it revision as in the model yml.

The five load-bearing pieces (all required; ablation below):
1. clipped linears - per-projection checkpoint activation clip bounds (16 blocks x 7 projections = 112 modules / 448 scalar bounds).
2. padded-patch masking + real image positions (Option-S) - pad patches excluded from attention.
3. image positions / pooling - per-patch (x,y); position-based pooling to soft tokens.
4. PLE pad substitution - image placeholder rows -> pad_token_id in the token-identity PLE path (HF-faithful; "both" is HF-divergent, ablation-only).
5. causal image spans - E2B/E4B image tokens attend causally (HF use_bidirectional_attention=None).

## Validation
E2B, MaxText NNX vs pinned HF 5.9.0, teacher-forced (gate: post_image max_KL <= 1.26e-3; argmax >= 0.995):

| fixture | segment | max_KL | argmax | gate |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| E2B structured | post_image (n=75) | 4.29e-05 | 1.000 | PASS |
| E2B natural | post_image (n~72) | 4.71e-05 | 1.000 | PASS |

Ablation (E2B structured - every component load-bearing):

| arm | post_image max_KL | image_span argmax | parity |
|---|---|---|---|
| full fix | 4.29e-05 | 1.000 | PASS |
| clip OFF | 1.195 | 0.596 | FAIL |
| padded-patch masking OFF | 0.328 | 0.762 | FAIL |
| PLE substitution OFF | 8.921 | 0.000 | FAIL (dominant) |
| PLE mode "both" (HF-divergent) | 13.44 | 0.346 | FAIL |

In-tree tests (CPU): tests/unit/gemma4_clip_linears_test.py (18) + tests/unit/gemma4_mm_contract_gate_test.py (8).

**Later integration validation (composite stack - integration provenance, NOT a claim that #4790 alone fixes
checkpoint-loader gaps):** production train.py completes forward -> backward -> optimizer-apply -> checkpoint-save
on real Gemma-4 E2B weights on the composite stack #4790 + #4807 (std-fidelity candidate) + an evidence-only
full-state checkpoint remap/splice bridge + stock train.py:
- CPU: loss 14.941 -> 11.596 (finite, decreasing); theta1 fresh-reload green; 448 vision clip bounds byte-identical theta0->theta1; 751/751 non-clip trainable leaves changed.
- TPU (tpu7x single host): loss 15.917 -> 14.020 (finite, decreasing); theta1 saved with populated opt_state; exit 0.

The params-only converted checkpoint does not yet enter stock load_parameters_path cleanly (a separate loader
69-leaf drop, tracked independently); the composite evidence used the splice bridge, which is NOT presented as
an upstream-supported loader path.

## Related work (separate PRs / follow-ups - each owns its own slice; do NOT fold together)
- #4807 - Gemma-4 vision std_bias/std_scale fidelity (standalone; #4790 forward parity does NOT depend on it).
- #4860 - Gemma-4 small HF export shape map (GEMMA4_SMALL_HF_WEIGHTS_TO_SHAPE vision + clip-bound coverage);
  composes with this PR's GEMMA4_SMALL_MAXTEXT_TO_HF_PARAM_MAPPING clip-bound targets.
- Shared-layer export completeness (S13) - a serving/checkpoint-completeness invariant tracked separately.

## Limitations
- E4B: vision-tower validated; full decoder E2E parity pending.
- Multimodal packing unsupported (fail-closed).
- Multi-image E2E: not yet in the in-tree matrix.
- The composite-stack backward/save evidence is integration provenance; the stock params-only loader gap is a separate issue.


## Gemma-4 small (E2B/E4B) vs large (26B/31B) — what differs, and why the new flags

The vision **tower** is shared (`vision_encoder_block: "gemma4"`, same `image_size_for_vit`). The E2B/E4B
config flags introduced here configure the *small-model image contract*; **each defaults to a no-op**, so
26B/31B and all other models are behaviorally unchanged.

| Aspect | E2B / E4B (small) | 26B / 31B (large) | Flag (default) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Per-layer embeddings (PLE) | Yes (`hidden_size_per_layer_input=256`) — needs image-row→pad substitution | No PLE path | `ple_pad_substitute_image_rows=False`, `ple_pad_mode="identity"`, `ple_pad_token_id=0`, `image_placeholder_token_id` (= `GEMMA4_TOKEN_PLACEHOLDER`) |
| Image-span attention | **Causal** (HF `use_bidirectional_attention=None`) | **Bidirectional** image spans | `use_bidirectional_image_attn=False` |
| Vision activation clip bounds | Checkpoint ships per-projection `{input,output}_{min,max}` (112 modules / 448 scalars) | Not present | `use_clipped_linears_for_vit=False` |
| Patch handling | Padded-patch / real per-patch positions supported (native-res / pan-and-scan); pad patches masked + position-pooled | Fixed-grid all-valid | `encoder_image_position_ids` present in data → opt-in; else legacy path |
| KV sharing | `num_kv_shared_layers` (E2B=20 / E4B=…) | n/a | model yml |

The **general** MM decode path (placeholder → `get_bidirectional_mask_vision` → `merge_mm_embeddings`) is
identical to 26B/31B and unchanged. The small-model additions live in (1) the PLE substitution
(`nnx_decoders._apply_gemma4_small_layers`, small-only) and (2) the padded-patch vision path
(`gemma4_vision.Gemma4VisionEncoderLayer`, opt-in via per-patch positions). All large-model and non-Gemma4
code paths take the default no-op branch.

title: Abhinavsing/elastic
SFT: tools rendering + developer role in chat-template preprocessing
body:
# Description

Add first-class support for **tool-calling SFT data** and the **`developer` role** to the
grain/HF chat-template preprocessing, so tool-augmented conversations render and mask correctly —
including across multi-turn conversations. Today the SFT pipeline only understands `system`/`user`/
`assistant` turns and a single primary data column; there is no way to feed tool/function
definitions to the chat template, the `developer` role is silently dropped, and a multi-turn
conversation loses its leading turn after the first round.

This change is fully opt-in and backward compatible: datasets without a `tools` column and without
`developer` turns behave exactly as before (`tools_column_name` defaults to `None`).

## What this adds

**Tools column.** A dataset may now provide an auxiliary `tools` column alongside `messages`
(supported column set `["messages", "tools"]`). The tools (a JSON string or a list of tool
definitions) are split off the primary data column, threaded through `apply_chat_template`, rendered
into every `apply_chat_template` call so tool-calling turns tokenize correctly, and dropped from the
dataset afterward. The chat-template wrapper also learns the `tool` role (tool results accumulate
into the current round without emitting an extra prompt/completion segment).

- `data_processing_utils.py`: `TOOLS_COLUMN = "tools"`; accept `["messages", "tools"]`.
- `hf_data_processing.py` / `grain_data_processing.py`: separate the `tools` column, thread it into
  `apply_chat_template`, drop it afterward (HF path also deserializes JSON string columns).
- `input_pipeline_utils.py`: `apply_chat_template` / `_get_completion_in_chat_template` accept the
  tools and pass them to every chat-template call; `enable_thinking=True` keeps the
  completion-boundary detection correct for thinking-channel templates (e.g. Gemma).

**Developer role.** `developer` is treated like `system` (a leading, index-0 role). Any other/
unknown role now raises instead of being silently ignored.

**Optional tools column (mixture-friendly).** `ParseFeatures` / `NormalizeFeatures` / `KeepFeatures`
treat `tools` as optional (`OPTIONAL_COLUMNS = {"tools"}`): a record without it is skipped rather
than raising, so a single grain mixture can blend tools and non-tools datasets. Required columns
still raise when missing.

**Multi-turn tools persistence.** Each new round is re-seeded with the leading system/developer turn
(`leading_msgs`) instead of clearing `round_msgs`. Clearing dropped the leading turn, so rounds 2+
of a multi-turn conversation rendered as a bare `<bos>user` prompt with no tools; under
completion-only loss that trained those rounds' tool-calls as (no-tools → call), which makes the
model emit spurious tool calls at inference. Re-seeding keeps the tools/persona rendered in every
round.

## Backward compatibility

- `tools_column_name` defaults to `None` → existing `messages`-only / `prompt,completion` /
  `question,answer` datasets are unchanged.
- The `developer` role and the optional-`tools` handling are additive; no existing behavior changes
  unless the data uses them.

## Shortcomings / future work

- Tools are rendered whenever present; there is no per-turn tool visibility control.
- `enable_thinking=True` is currently unconditional (kept for correct completion-boundary detection
  on thinking-channel templates); making it configurable is a possible follow-up.

# Tests

The change preserves the existing `apply_chat_template` signature for non-tools callers, so the
existing SFT data-processing tests (`tests/post_training/unit/sft_data_processing_test.py`) continue
to exercise the system/user/assistant paths for the qwen3 / llama2 / gemma4 tokenizers:

```bash
python -m pytest tests/post_training/unit/sft_data_processing_test.py -v
```

The new control-flow (developer role, unknown-role error, `tool`-role accumulation, multi-turn
leading-turn re-seeding, and the optional-`tools` skipping) was validated against the migrated
functions with a mock tokenizer:
- `developer` accepted as a leading (index-0) turn with tools passed through; `developer` at a
  non-zero index raises.
- an unsupported role raises (the new `else` branch).
- a `tool` message accumulates into the round and emits no extra segment.
- round 2 of a multi-turn conversation still renders the leading `developer` turn + tools (not a
  bare user prompt).
- `NormalizeFeatures`/`KeepFeatures` skip an absent `tools` column but still raise on an absent
  required column.

title: Keep fused MoE weights intact through FSDP gather
body:
# Description

Keep prefused MoE input weights intact through the FSDP all-gather, avoiding an unnecessary weight slice/concatenate sequence and improving DeepSeek V3 performance by approximately 1.5% on GB300.

Previously, `prefuse_moe_weights` stored the two MoE input projections as one `[experts, embed, 2 * mlp]` tensor, but the sparse MoE path split this tensor into `w0` and `w1` before entering `shard_map`. This caused FSDP to all-gather the two halves separately, after which they were concatenated again immediately before the grouped GEMM.

This change passes the prefused weight through `shard_map` intact. The sparse MoE path now performs:

1. One FSDP all-gather of the `[experts, embed, 2 * mlp]` weight.
2. One grouped GEMM producing `[tokens, 2 * mlp]`.
3. A split of the activation output immediately before the SwiGLU activation.

This removes the pre-GEMM weight slicing and avoids the second independent FSDP all-gather. The implementation also preserves the fused weight through two-stage FSDP all-gather and applies the appropriate partition specifications to the combined tensor.

The optimization is restricted to sparse matmul with prefused weights, outside quantized serving and weight-sparsity paths. Existing split-weight paths remain unchanged as fallbacks. There is no change to the checkpoint format or default behavior because the optimization is controlled by the existing `prefuse_moe_weights` option.

# Tests

Tested with DeepSeek V3 training on NVIDIA GB300 using:

```yaml
prefuse_moe_weights: true
sparse_matmul: true
```

Compared against the same workload, configuration, and container without this change:

- HLO/profile inspection confirmed that the prefused weight remains intact through FSDP all-gather.
- The unnecessary pre-GEMM weight slice operations were removed.
- The two independent input-weight all-gathers were replaced by one combined all-gather.
- End-to-end training performance improved by approximately 1.5%.
- `git diff --check` passes.

title: feat(ci): exclude expensive notebook tests from analyze_code_changes fail-safe
body:
# Description

When `git diff` against `origin/$BASE_REF` fails or returns empty in a Pull Request, `.github/scripts/analyze_code_changes.sh` triggers a fail-safe. Previously, this fail-safe enabled all test suites including `run_notebooks` (`set_test_flags "true" "true"`). 

When `run_notebooks="true"` was emitted for an empty/failed diff, `.github/workflows/run_jupyter_notebooks.yml` detected 0 modified notebooks and defaulted to executing **all 7 active notebooks** simultaneously across self-hosted `v6e-8` TPU runners (`linux-x86-ct6e-180-8tpu`). Because the runner pool only has 4 runners, this saturated 100% of the TPU runner capacity, causing massive queueing delays for all PRs.

This PR makes the following improvements:
1. **Refines the fail-safe flags**: Calls `set_test_flags "true" "false"`, keeping all core test suites (`run_tests`, `run_pretrain_tests`, `run_posttrain_tests`, `run_pathways_tests`, `run_gpu_tests`) enabled for regression safety while strictly disabling expensive notebook tests. This aligns with the unmatched code fallback in line 214 of `analyze_code_changes.sh`.
2. **Hardens git diff target resolution**: Adds fallback resolution for `${DIFF_TARGET}` (`origin/$BASE_REF` -> `FETCH_HEAD`).
3. **Improves observability**: Captures and logs `git diff` errors (`Warning: git diff encountered an error: ...`) instead of silently swallowing them with `2>/dev/null`.

# Tests

Tested using simulation test harness across all execution paths:
1. **Scheduled run (`EVENT_NAME="schedule"`)**: Verified all test suites and notebooks run (`run_tests=true`, `run_notebooks=true`).
2. **PR with empty diff / fail-safe**: Verified core test suites are enabled but notebook tests are disabled (`run_tests=true`, `run_notebooks=false`).
3. **PR with git diff error**: Verified warning is printed, core test suites are enabled, and notebook tests are disabled (`run_tests=true`, `run_notebooks=false`).
4. **PR with real changes**: Verified domain-specific test selection continues to function as expected.
5. **Syntax verification**: `bash -n .github/scripts/analyze_code_changes.sh` passed cleanly.
